build.detail: Run on node1 from lean-causal/. `taskset -c 0-11 lake env lean -DwarningAsError=true Causal/Ladder/Dual.lean`: rc 0, 1.2 s. The same on Causal/Ladder/DualTest.lean: rc 0, 12.2 s. Oleans of Dual (07:41:19), Rules (07:41:20) and DualTest (07:41:32) are newer than the sources (Dual.lean 07:41:06, DualTest.lean 07:35:13), so those runs tested the shipped Dual. lake build was not run, as instructed. `grep -nwE 'sorry|admit|axiom|native_decide'` on Dual.lean and DualTest.lean finds nothing. #print axioms, from a probe written to the campaign directory and deleted afterwards: futureOneConnected_of_dual and futureOneConnected_dual give [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]; locallyStronglyCausal_of_dual and locallyStronglyCausal_dual give [propext, Quot.sound]. A run_cmd count gives 46 theorems in Causal.LadderDual. The tactician's 84-command #check @ / #print axioms probe of the 42 older theorems, rerun now, matches its pre-edit snapshot /tmp/tac-dfoc/sig_before.txt byte for byte (120 lines; 26 x [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], 16 x [propext, Quot.sound]). The Lean diff of Dual.lean only adds lines, so this is expected.

checks.1_rules_correct: Dual.lean:262-272. Each rule is .1 or .2 of the library iff. Causal.Causality.dual_futureOneConnected : C.dual.FutureOneConnected <-> C.FutureOneConnected (TimelikeHomotopy.lean:474, = dual_futureOneConnectedOn at W = top, from FutureOneConnectedOn.dual :460). Causal.Causality.dual_locallyStronglyCausal : C.dual.LocallyStronglyCausal <-> C.LocallyStronglyCausal (DiamondConfinement.lean:400, simp through dual_stronglyCausalOn :396). So *_of_dual : C.dual.P -> C.P is .1 and *_dual : C.P -> C.dual.P is .2. The #check @ types are exactly those, with binders {M} [TopologicalSpace M] {C}. The ladder's Lean forms are programme/ladder.toml:1232 lean = "Causal.Causality.FutureOneConnected" and :1312 lean = "Causal.Causality.LocallyStronglyCausal", which are the predicates the rules conclude. Attribute blocks: the *_of_dual names are in the plain `aesop safe forward (rule_sets := [CausalLadder])` block (:304-311, line :309) and the *_dual names in the `safe forward (pattern := Causality.dual C)` block (:313-319, line :318). Each sits right after hasChronalNeighbourEverywhere_of_dual / _dual, its precedent, with the same pattern Causality.dual C. That makes 23 plain + 21 patterned = 44 CausalLadder rules.
checks.2_kb0221_no_cycle: With tools/ladder.py on the current lean_index: import_chain(Causal.DiamondConfinement, imports, Causal.Ladder.Rules) = None; the same for Causal.TimelikeHomotopy and Causal.Ladder.Dual; model_path None for all three; dual_import(index) = (True, None). Dual's Causal closure (36 modules + itself = 37) is a subset of Rules' (53 + itself = 54). Causal.DiamondConfinement, TimelikeHomotopy, CausalIsoInvariance and GXStructure were already in Rules' closure, because Rules.lean imports Causal.DiamondConfinement directly. A comment-stripped grep for causal_ladder over the source of every module in Rules' closure hits only Causal.Ladder.Basic, which defines the macro (Basic.lean:88) and does not use it. ChronalTarentin, CurvesExtend and Ladder.Dual mention it in comments only. Causal.Ladder.* in Dual's closure: Basic only (plus LadderLocal, which is not a Ladder.* module).
checks.3_dualtest_is_script_output: `python3 -I -B lean-causal/campaign/T-tac-ladder-dual/dual_closure.py shipped /tmp/audit-dfoc/DualTest.lean` (rc 0) is byte-identical to the tree's Causal/Ladder/DualTest.lean (diff empty; both sha256 e3a37f1d4e840a83496800e2477601bcd8f5679908e01ce1508485bdae5e949f, as REPORT.json states). It was run on the ladder committed at 4a78ce34 (programme/ladder.toml has no working-tree diff), so DualTest agrees with the committed ladder. `counts` reproduces REPORT's numbers: 21 properties, 19 two-sided; 21 bare emitted edges; derived 68, refuted 768, unknown 46, total 882; no same-side pair derived only through the dual rules; 7 conjunctive. The 46 unknown pairs match REPORT's list (19x2 curves_extend pairs + 8). dual_closure.py itself is unchanged (no git diff); it stops refusing because check_dual now finds the four names. Against HEAD's DualTest: 470 -> 561 examples, 380 -> 463 fail_if_success. Comparing example blocks as multisets, all 470 old blocks are present verbatim and 91 are new. Refutation comments: 376 -> 459, none lost, 139 name another witness, 83 are new pairs. 82 of the new pairs involve the new nodes. The other one is chronal_neighbours(C) =/=> absolutely_minimal(C.dual) by Causal.densCausality_separates, which states ChronalNeighbours and not AbsolutelyMinimal (DensSeparates.lean:199-202), so the witness is correct. Spot checks. Positives at :167 (StronglyCausal C |- LocallyStronglyCausal C.dual) and :289-295 (the four self-pairs) close. Negatives at :388 (IsCausal C =/=> FutureOneConnected C.dual, Flat.spaceCylinder_separates), :1990 and :2042 (FutureOneConnected C =/=> IsCausal / LocallyStronglyCausal of C.dual). Their witnesses check out in Lean: symmRationalLine_separates_locallyStronglyCausal states FutureOneConnected and not IsCausal; galileoCurve_separates states FutureOneConnected, not LocallyStronglyCausal and not StronglyCausal; lightlikeLine_separates_futureOneConnected states FutureOneConnected and not HasChronalNeighbourEverywhere. All 463 negatives, rewritten by negatives_plain.py into /tmp and run with -DmaxErrors=100000, give 463 errors, all 'failed to prove the goal after exhaustive search', none at a limit. With the four rules erased (erase_aesop_rules after the `open Causal Causal.Causality` line of a /tmp copy), exactly 4 errors remain, at the four self-pairs (DualTest :289, :291, :293, :295). The exact mode (`exact /tmp/...`) is byte-identical to campaign/.../DualExact.lean (882 examples, 814 fail_if_success) and elaborates under -DwarningAsError=true (rc 0, 18.9 s). same_side.py: '21 properties, 3122 premise sets (each side): 0 with a same-side detour', so Dual's SCOPE claim holds. ProbesPos.lean closes under -DwarningAsError=true. ProbesNeg.lean gives 8 x exhaustive search.
checks.4_nothing_else_changed: `git diff --quiet` on Causal/Ladder/Rules.lean and Test.lean succeeds, so neither changed. `python3 -I -B tools/ladder.py emit-lean --dry-run` (the subcommand exists, tools/ladder.py:1369 and :1424, and writes nothing; md5 of both files is the same before and after) reports both 'unchanged'. Timing check of the docstring's 'no measurable time' sentence: Test.lean with the four rules and with them erased, 2 interleaved rounds, 7.90-8.13 s against 7.98-8.08 s. That is within noise, so the claim holds.

findings.what: Process deviation with no effect on any result. The builds ran as `taskset -c 0-23 lake build ...` (Dual, Rules and DualTest, then the whole `Causal`). The tactics-builder protocol pins to cores 0-11 (.claude/agents/tactics-builder.md:39-40), and CAMPAIGN.md says never to run `lake build Causal`. Rebuilding the 39 modules downstream of an exclusive edit to Dual.lean is what the precedent did (T-tac-dual-has-chronal-neighbour, `taskset -c 0-11 lake build Causal`, audited clean), and the dispatch accepts it. Only the 24-core width departs from house practice, while other loops' leases (atlas, restate) were live on node1.
findings.fix: None for this target. A later exclusive tactic target should keep taskset -c 0-11.

notes: No major finding. The four rules are exactly .1/.2 of Causality.dual_futureOneConnected and Causality.dual_locallyStronglyCausal, registered like the has_chronal_neighbour precedent (plain block; patterned block with Causality.dual C). The new import makes no cycle, and no module in Rules' closure uses causal_ladder (kb/0221). DualTest.lean is the script's output byte for byte, rerun to /tmp on the committed ladder of 4a78ce34; it builds under warningAsError, and its 463 negatives fail by exhaustion. Rules.lean and Test.lean are unchanged, and emit-lean --dry-run reports both unchanged. Axioms are standard, with no sorry, admit, axiom or native_decide. Only the dispatched files and the campaign directory were touched.
